en: Majjhima Nikāya 42:
The Verañjaka Sutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, some brahmin householders from Verañjā were staying at Sāvatthī on some business.
The brahmin householders from Verañjā heard:
“Sirs, the ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from the Sakyan clan, is staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
A fine report concerning that venerable Gotama has spread abroad:

‘Indeed, that Blessed One is an arahant, perfectly enlightened, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, fortunate, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’”

Thus, having realized for himself through direct higher knowledge this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, he makes it known.
He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life, entirely complete and pure.
It is indeed good to see such Arahants.”
Then the brahmin householders of Verañjā approached the Blessed One.
Having approached, some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side;
some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and having concluded the polite and courteous conversation, sat down to one side; others...
They extended their joined palms toward the Blessed One and sat down to one side;
some, having announced their names and clans in the presence of the Blessed One, sat down to one side; others sat down to one side in silence.
Seated to one side, the brahmin householders of Verañjā said this to the Blessed One:

“Master Gotama, what is the cause, what is the reason why some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell?
And what, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason why some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world?”

“Householders, it is because of unrighteous conduct and improper conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, perdition, even in hell.
Householders, it is because of righteous conduct and proper conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world.
“We do not understand the detailed meaning of this statement made by Master Gotama in brief, which has not been explained in detail. [Please explain it to us.]”

“It would be well if Master Gotama would teach us the Dhamma in such a way that we might understand in detail the meaning of what has been stated by Master Gotama in brief, without its detailed meaning having been explained.
“In that case, householders, listen and attend closely; I shall speak.
“Yes, sir,” the brahmin householders of Verañjā replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
"Householders, one who acts contrary to the Dhamma and acts unrighteously does so in three ways by way of body, in four ways by way of speech, and in three ways by way of mind.
And how, householders, does one act contrary to the Dhamma and act unrighteously in three ways by way of body?"
In this case, householders, a certain person is a destroyer of life. He is cruel, bloody-handed, intent on killing and striking, and lacks compassion for living beings.
Furthermore, he is a taker of what is not given; he takes by way of theft whatever belongs to another, the property and belongings of others.
Moreover, he engages in sexual misconduct; he has sexual relations with women who are protected by their mothers... [and so forth] with such women as these.
In this way, householders, one is an unrighteous and immoral person in three ways by means of the body.
And how, householders, is one an unrighteous and immoral person in four ways by means of speech?
Here, householders, a certain person is a speaker of falsehood; whether in an assembly... he is one who speaks deliberately lying words.
Furthermore, he is one who speaks divisively; having heard something here, he reports it there...
he utters speech that causes dissension. Furthermore, he is one who speaks harshly; he utters such speech as is bitter, rough, and so forth.
Furthermore, he is one who indulges in idle chatter; he speaks at the wrong time... speech that is limitless, unbeneficial, and not connected to the goal.
In this way, householders, one is unrighteous and immoral in four ways by means of speech.
And how, householders, is one unrighteous and immoral in three ways by means of the mind?
Here, householders, a certain person is covetous... [and so on] ... ‘May what belongs to him become mine.’”
Furthermore, he has a mind of ill will and a corrupt intention, thinking: “May these beings be slain… or may they cease to exist!
Moreover, he holds wrong view and possesses perverted vision, thinking:
“There is no giving, there is no sacrifice… nor do those who have realized this for themselves proclaim it.”
In this way, householders, one acts contrary to the Dhamma and behaves unrighteously in three ways by means of the mind.

It is because of such conduct contrary to the Dhamma and unrighteous behavior, householders, that some beings here, with the breakup of the body after death, are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or hell.

Householders, one acts according to the Dhamma and behaves righteously in three ways by means of the body; one acts according to the Dhamma and behaves righteously in four ways by means of speech; and one acts according to the Dhamma and behaves righteously in three ways by means of the mind.
And how, householders, does one act righteously and live according to the Dhamma in three ways by way of the body?

Here, householders, a certain person, having abandoned the taking of life, abstains from taking life; he lays aside the rod and the weapon, dwells with a sense of shame and compassion, and is sympathetic toward the welfare of all living beings.
Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given; he does not take by theft what belongs to another, what has not been given, and which is considered stolen.
"Having abandoned sexual misconduct... he does not engage in improper conduct with women who are protected by others.
In this way, householders, one is a practitioner of Dhamma and a practitioner of equanimity in three ways by means of the body.
And how, householders, is one a practitioner of Dhamma and a practitioner of equanimity in four ways by means of speech?"
In this case, householders, a certain person, having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech. Whether in an assembly... [and so on] ...he does not speak consciously lying words.
Having abandoned malicious speech... he speaks words that create harmony.
Having abandoned harsh speech... he speaks such words as are gentle.
Having abandoned idle chatter... [he speaks] at the proper time, what is meaningful, measured, and connected with the goal.
In this way, householders, one is a practitioner of the Dhamma and a practitioner of equanimity in four ways by means of speech.
And how, householders, is one a practitioner of the Dhamma and a practitioner of equanimity in three ways by means of the mind?
In this case, householders, a certain person is free from covetousness. He does not covet the wealth and possessions of others, thinking: "O, that what belongs to another were mine!

Furthermore, he is of a mind without ill will and of intentions that are not corrupt, thinking: "May these beings be free from enmity, free from affliction, free from distress, and may they maintain themselves in happiness.
Moreover, he possesses right view and has an undistorted perspective.
‘There is what is given; there is what is sacrificed... having realized it for themselves through direct knowledge, they make it known.
It is in this way, householders, that one is a practitioner of Dhamma and a practitioner of equanimity in three ways by means of the mind.

It is for the sake of such practice of Dhamma and practice of equanimity, householders, that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappear in a happy destination, in a heavenly world.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously should wish:

"Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of wealthy kṣatriyas," it is indeed possible that, after the breakup of the body, after death, he will arise in the company of wealthy kṣatriyas.
For what reason?
Because he is one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously should so desire:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, following death,
I might arise in the company of wealthy brahmins...
[or] wealthy householders!’— it is indeed possible that, after the breakup of the body, following death, he will arise in the company of wealthy householders.
For what reason?
Because he is one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives in accordance with the Dhamma.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives in accordance with the Dhamma, should so desire:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings!’—
it is indeed possible that, after the breakup of the body, after death, he will arise in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings. And why is that?
For he is one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives righteously.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives righteously, should wish:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might [be reborn] among the Tāvatiṃsa devas..."
...of the Yāma devas ...
of the Tusita devas ...
of the Nimmānarati devas ...
‘May I be reborn in companionship with the Paranimmitavasavatti devas… or with the Brahmakāyika devas’—
it is indeed possible that, with the breakup of the body after death, he will be reborn in companionship with the Brahmakāyika devas.
For what reason?
Because he is one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously should so desire:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the Ābhā devas!’—
it is indeed possible that, after the breakup of the body, after death, he will arise in the company of the Ābhā devas.
For what reason?
For such a person is one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously.
Householders, if a person living according to the Dhamma and living righteously should wish:
“Oh, that upon the dissolution of the body, after death, I might [be reborn] among the gods of Limited Radiance... [and so on].”
...of the gods of Immeasurable Radiance,
...of the gods of Streaming Radiance,
...of the gods of Limited Beauty...
...of the Appamāṇasubha devas ...
of the Subhakiṇha devas ...
of the Vehapphala devas ...
...of the Aviha devas...
of the Atappa devas...
of the Sudassa devas...
...of the Sudassī devas ...
of the Akaniṭṭha devas ...
of the devas who have reached the base of infinite space ...

‘May I be reborn into the company of the devas who have attained the base of infinite consciousness… the devas who have attained the base of nothingness… the devas who have attained the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.’”
It is indeed possible that, with the breakup of the body after death, he might be reborn into the company of the devas who have attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
Why is that? Because he is one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously should wish:
"O, that by the destruction of the taints, I might dwell in this very life having realized for myself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom,

and having entered upon them," it is indeed possible that he, by the destruction of the taints, will dwell in this very life having realized for himself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon them.
"And for what reason?
Because he is one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives with equanimity.
When this was said, the brahmin householders of Verañjā said this to the Blessed One:
“Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama!

Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms; [so it has been done by Master Gotama].”
"In this very way, the Dhamma has been proclaimed by the venerable Gotama in many ways.
We go for refuge to the venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
May the venerable Gotama accept us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life shall last."
The Verañjakasutta, the second, is finished.
